newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar loses more ground with NY bears.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar loses more ground with NY bears.

text.p: London's March white sugar contract was reluctant to show its head above the $300 parapet as all values compounded their earlier weakness and hovered around intraday lows.
Earlier, mixed sellers moved in anticipation of weakness on the raws, and the expected lower New York open sparked even more selling, traders said.
"It (London) has stayed under a bit of pressure with New York coming in lower...it looks weak again," said one.
Some March white premium offer orders were noted at $69.00 and $69.50, indicating a widening arbitrage on the spot position as the trading level for March/March was nearer $68.00, traders said.

At 1711 GMT March was $2.50 lower at $298.20 and May down $1.50 at $298.70. Other months were lower and the structure of the futures board was mixed as the spot position moved into contango against May.

Volume was a solid 2,272 lots, more than half of which was in the spot position. A few hundred lots of against actuals trades were cited in March to boost the overall volume and the nearby March/May spread was trading at between flat and 50 cents.

In Colombia, the six-day-old dock workers' strike at Buenaventura has paralysed the export of at least 27,000 tonnes of sugar, with 17,000 tonnes in bulk sugar in containers and another 10,000 tonnes in 200,000 50-kg sacks.
Turkey sold 50,000 tonnes of sugar to local firms Lebsan and Fisan under last week's tender.
European traders said they were still awaiting news of Libya's recent tender to buy white sugar.
Paris futures were also lower but only the two nearby months were traded in turnover of 792 lots.
March was down $1.60 at $298.50 and May down $1.60 at $298.50.
